name: Spicy Eggplant Shakshuka
why: A vibrant Middle Eastern-inspired skillet loaded with roasted eggplant, zucchini, and bell peppers in a spicy tomato sauce, poached with eggs. Peak summer vegetables meet smoky heat — perfect for late-August when eggplant is at its best.
author: Henry
ingredients: 1 medium zucchini, diced into 1/2" cubes (about 1 1/2 cups)
1/2 large eggplant, diced into 1/2" cubes (about 4 cups)
1/2 bell pepper (red, yellow, or orange), seeded and diced
1/2 cup chicken broth or vegetable broth

steps: In a large, deep skillet (cast iron is ideal), heat 4 Tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat.
Once the oil is hot, add diced zucchini, eggplant, onion, and bell pepper.
Season with 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Sauté, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes or until vegetables are soft and lightly golden.
Add the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, and chicken broth. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Add the pressed garlic cloves and 2 tsp Tabasco sauce.
Taste the sauce and add another splash of Tabasco if you prefer more heat.
Simmer on low boil for 2 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Crack each egg into a small ramekin, then gently drop it into the sauce around the edge of the pan (6-8 eggs total).
Season the eggs lightly with salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Arrange the baby spinach around the eggs, pushing leaves slightly into the sauce.
Cover the pan and simmer over low heat for 6-8 minutes.
The whites should be fully set; yolks will be runny (adjust time for firmer yolks).
Remove from heat — note that eggs will continue cooking if the lid stays on.
Serve directly from the skillet with crusty bread or a baguette for soaking up the sauce.

pro_tips: Eggplant absorbs oil like a sponge — salt the diced eggplant for 15 minutes and pat dry before cooking to reduce oil absorption and improve texture.
For extra richness, stir a dollop of Greek yogurt or labneh into each serving right before eating. The cool creaminess balances the spicy sauce perfectly.
